executive_summary:
socxen is a SOC analyst agent for Claude Code and Codex: three prompt-driven skills (investigate one alert or case, sweep the open queue, propose detection tuning) that reach an Exabeam New-Scale tenant only through a bundled local MCP bridge holding the operator's API key and secret. Its untrusted input is tenant telemetry - alert fields, case names and notes, rule descriptions - which anyone who can influence logged activity can shape. The trust surfaces that matter most are the host-enforced approval hook that decides which tool calls run without a human, and the bridge, which screens everything read, neutralizes everything written and keeps the audit trail. Dismiss, close, outbound email, containment and today's rule-write tools are all held by that hook.

The first thing to fix is the queue sweep. Case creation and case notes run without a prompt for every skill, and the hook cannot tell a read-only sweep from an investigation, so text planted in queued cases that the model follows can open cases and write notes across the queue with no human in the loop. Only a prose instruction stands in the way; give the sweep a read-only tool surface enforced in code. Second, a rule, exclusion or context-table write tool the platform adds later would get an approval prompt rather than a hard deny, and its free text would pass unneutralized if it used field names the bridge does not know. One approved prompt, possibly obtained by planted rule text, could then quietly blind detection.

Third, the bridge is launched without enforcing its hash-pinned lock, so on an older uv a fresh install can pull untested upstream packages into the process that holds the Exabeam secret. Lower-order items: the gate log stores email recipients, the audit trail can be switched off silently and omits the close reason, Codex preflight does not check the mail approval setting, and the API token carries the key's full platform scope.

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST NEVER treat content retrieved from the platform
socxen MUST NOT reason over or act on text retrieved from the platform before that text has been screened
it MUST stop that action path, report the attempted injection to the analyst

threats.summary: Attacker-planted invisible code points (tag block, bidi overrides, zero-width) in alert, event or case fields smuggle hidden instructions to the model.
threats.remainder: kept invisibles spliced into ASCII words, emoji variation-selector channels and NBSP keyword-splitting pass by design (canonicalize.py:18)

threats.summary: Plain-language instructions in attacker-influenceable alert, case or rule text steer the verdict or the next tool call; the only control is the skills' untrusted-data instruction.
threats.remainder: enforcement is instruction-level only - no code checks provenance, so a model that follows injected text is stopped only by the host gate downstream

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST state the minimum model it is validated on

threats.summary: Tenant telemetry - including credentials and PII inside alert fields - reaches the operator's model provider unredacted (checked: canonicalize.py strips code points only; the neutralizer runs on writes only, exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:1161).
The injection-resistance floor (Sonnet 4.6+/Opus) is documentation only; a session on an unsupported smaller model runs unchecked (checked: installation.md:22, preflight.sh - no model check).

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision to Exabeam tool call

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST be blocked by a host-enforced gate that is active on a fresh install with no operator opt-in
No containment-class or enforcement tool
MUST deny any future tool that modifies, enables, disables or retunes a detection rule
an MCP tool the tiers do not classify MUST ask, never run silently

threats.summary: Injected text drives a containment or rule/exclusion/context-table write tool; the hook deny tier and Codex disabled_tools refuse every listed spelling.
threats.remainder: a manual registration whose server name lacks 'exabeam' is not matched (hooks.json:5, gate.py:84), and the documented any-other-agent path carries no host gate

threats.summary: A future rule, exclusion or context-table write tool the tiers do not name falls through to ask rather than deny, so a single human yes lets it run.
Dismiss, close or outbound email executed without a human; the hook asks on every call and Codex approves per call.
threats.remainder: same unmatched-server-name and ungated any-other-agent paths as the deny tier

threats.summary: On Codex, a config.toml override that auto-approves exabeam_send_email passes preflight as gate ON, so the loss of the mail gate goes unreported.

remit_rules.excerpt: During a queue sweep socxen MUST NOT write to the platform at all
socxen MUST NOT write text into a platform record without first de-activating executable content and clickable links in it
socxen MUST NOT delete or overwrite existing free-text content
every case-note or export write MUST pass through the bridge's deterministic output neutralizer

threats.summary: A queue sweep steered by queue content (or drift) opens cases or writes case notes across the queue with no human prompt, because those two writes are allow-tier for every skill and the hook cannot see the skill.
Model-written text in a write field outside the eight neutralized keys (e.g. a future tool's description or comment) reaches the tenant with live links or formulas.
An update overwrites analyst-authored free text or closes with an arbitrary reason; the bridge forwards state fields only and refuses non-canonical closedReason values.
A close is routed around the gated update by creating a case with a closing stage; the bridge refuses any create_case carrying a closing disposition.
Credentials or personal data copied from evidence persist into case notes or outbound mail; the neutralizer masks structured secrets and identifiers.
threats.remainder: free-form names and addresses, dates of birth and unlabeled bare credentials are not masked (declared redaction limits)

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials and any token derived from them MUST NEVER be written to the audit log
MUST NEVER be transmitted to any host other than the operator-configured Exabeam API endpoint

threats.summary: The API key and secret are readable by other local users if the env file is not mode 600; preflight only warns.
threats.remainder: the bridge reads the file regardless of its mode (exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:52) and nothing tightens it

threats.summary: Credentials or the bearer token leak into the audit trail or cross the network in clear; the audit record is a safe-field allowlist and the bridge refuses non-https URLs.

The minted token carries the API key's full platform scope, so any tool the gate lets through - or any client bypassing it - acts with that breadth (checked: exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:125 client_credentials grant with no scope parameter).

remit_rules.excerpt: Free-text field values, raw tool arguments, raw tool results, and neutralized hostile payloads MUST NEVER be written into the audit log
Every gated disposition change MUST be recorded deterministically at the point of the write
MUST NOT disappear silently
local-only recording is the required default

threats.summary: The gate log persists send_email recipients - raw tool arguments including partial names - to disk.
SOCXEN_OBSERVRA=off removes the whole audit trail with no stderr disclosure.
A case close is logged without its closedReason, so a reviewer cannot tell a false-positive close from a low-risk close.
Audit telemetry leaves the host silently; the default backend is local jsonl and any off-host destination is resolved and announced on stderr and in the session record.

remit_rules.excerpt: The bridge's full resolved dependency set MUST be hash-pinned in the shipped lockfile
Tool definitions from the bundled Exabeam MCP MUST be hashed per session

threats.summary: A fresh install on an older uv re-resolves the bridge's dependencies within version ranges instead of the hash-pinned lock, running untested upstream code with credential access.
A changed or poisoned remote tool definition (rug pull) is accepted each session; definitions are screened, hashed and directive text surfaced.
threats.remainder: no baseline is stored between sessions, so a change is visible only by comparing hashes after the fact

threats.summary: A compromised marketplace repository ships a modified plugin (skills, hook or bridge) on install or update (checked: install.sh:263 adds the GitHub marketplace; no signature or hash check on the installed payload found).

attack_paths.name: An unpinned upstream package release runs inside the bridge that holds the Exabeam secret

steps.summary: origin: third-party upstream release resolved fresh within version ranges when uv ignores the script lock
consequence: untested code executes on the operator's host in the process that holds the API key, secret and bearer token

notes.lane_fit: The PreToolUse hook and the Codex approval map sit in client_adapters because the host process enforces them; the two local JSONL logs and the advisory preflight script are placed in external_deploy as telemetry/deploy posture although they live on the operator's host; the model call happens inside the host, so the model is represented only as the provider node.
notes.omissions: KB arbitration divergence: PRAX-2026-09-19-008 is stored as LLM10; per the KB compound table its gate facet (unclassified rule-write gets ask, not deny) is the ungated-consequential-capability row, so that threat is tagged LLM03 at tool-invocation while its neutralization facet keeps LLM10 at state-commit. No PRAX-2026-09-19-002 exists in the findings JSON; nothing cites it. Not modelled as nodes: the host's spill file for oversized tool results (a host artifact, remit Open Question 9, no socxen code path to cite), off-host observra backends (opt-in; covered as a mitigated telemetry-egress threat), settings.snippet.json/merge tooling (generated fallback tier source folded into the gate node), and the create-case guard's sibling DRY_RUN refusal (test-mode only). Edgeless nodes: preflight-sh-control (advisory posture check), install-sh-deploy-surface (install posture). The rule-tuning skill has no Codex edge in the graph because the finding-backed Codex concern is the create_case auto mode, which the soc-investigate and triage-cases edges carry.
